assessment.nobel_worthiness: Task-based and skill-biased accounts of technology, together with the measured local labour-market effects of import competition, changed how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality, labour demand and adjustment. The work combines new data, transparent quasi-experimental designs and an explanatory framework, and it has shaped a very large empirical and policy literature.
assessment.attribution: The task and skill-demand strand is most closely tied to Autor and Katz. The trade-shock strand is most closely tied to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. A three-person limit forces a choice between Dorn and Katz, and Katz's contribution partly overlaps with work by prior laureates. Acemoglu, a prior laureate, shaped the task framework and is not on this credited list.
assessment.maturity: The work is about two decades old, with many replications, extensions and some contested reinterpretations. That is enough time to judge its durable influence.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat the technology and trade-shock strands as a single discovery.
The choice of Katz versus Dorn, and the overlap with Goldin's prize on labour-market and skill history.
Debate over how persistent and how large the China-shock effects were.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, interest-rate rules and the microfounded analysis of monetary policy is the standard apparatus of central banks. It has had unusually large practical impact together with deep theoretical content.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely spread. Calvo (price setting), Taylor (staggered contracts and the rule), Woodford (the integrated framework), Gali and Gertler (the empirical and policy analysis) and Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets (estimated DSGE models) all have strong claims. Limiting the award to three is difficult, and leaving out Calvo or Gertler is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: The framework is more than twenty-five years old and in continuous use. The post-2021 inflation episode has prompted renewed debate but has not displaced it.
uncertainties: Which three of the eight credited names best capture the conceptual core.
Possible overlap with earlier prizes on rational expectations and monetary policy.
The framework's performance in the recent inflation episode.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data have turned intergenerational mobility into a precisely measured, geographically detailed quantity. The work also links that measurement to causal neighbourhood and policy effects and has had a large impact on research agendas and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is clearly central. Hendren (neighbourhood exposure effects) and Friedman (mobility data and tax-record work) are the most plausible co-recipients, and Katz's role overlaps with another strand on this list. Credit within large collaborations is hard to disentangle.
assessment.maturity: The core results are roughly a decade old. Replication on other national data is substantial but incomplete, and the long-run policy lessons are still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether some findings, especially on neighbourhood causal effects, will hold up over time.
How the committee would divide credit across a large collaboration.
The work may be seen as too recent relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit studies gave labour economics a credible design for measuring discrimination in hiring. The resume field experiment and related work became a template for a large literature and changed public and legal debate. It is a clean case of design-based empirical contribution.
assessment.attribution: The influential résumé study is credited to Bertrand and Mullainathan. Charles has a distinct line of work on taste-based discrimination and measurement, but the three-name set is less cohesive than the two-name core. The audit-study tradition also predates them.
assessment.maturity: The study dates from 2004 and has been replicated across many countries and settings. Its influence is well established.
uncertainties: Whether the original design contribution outweighs the earlier audit-study tradition.
Debate over what the callback gaps identify, namely taste, statistical discrimination or employer beliefs.
The breadth of the contribution compared with candidates that built a full framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learning methods adapted for causal inference, including heterogeneous treatment effects, double or debiased estimation and high-dimensional methods with valid inference, have become widely used tools across empirical fields. The methodological contribution is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Athey and Chernozhukov are the clearest leaders of the two main strands. Wager is a key coauthor on causal forests and is more junior. Credit is also shared with the wider statistics and machine-learning community.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are from roughly 2016 to 2018. Adoption is rapid, but the literature is still developing, and the long-run value is less settled than for older methods.
uncertainties: Possible prematurity relative to older candidates.
How much of the credit belongs to economics rather than statistics and computer science.
Overlap with Chernozhukov's other methodological work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to open-economy macroeconomics, the Obstfeld–Rogoff framework and the exchange-rate disconnect puzzles gave international macroeconomics a coherent microfounded basis and set a research agenda that remains active. Policy influence is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair for the framework and the puzzles. Rogoff also appears in a separate candidate on financial crises, so the committee would need to decide where his credit is best placed.
assessment.maturity: The core work is from the 1990s and has had decades of testing. Some puzzles remain unresolved, which is a strength for agenda-setting but a weakness for confirmation.
uncertainties: How the committee would treat Rogoff's overlapping credit with another candidate.
Whether the disconnect puzzles count as a confirmed discovery or an open problem.
Overlap with earlier prizes in open-economy macroeconomics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microfoundations and evidence on agglomeration, the economics of cities, housing supply and sorting address central questions of productivity, inequality and regional disparity. The work is rigorous and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Glaeser, Duranton and Puga cover the main strands: urban growth and housing, agglomeration microfoundations and the empirical estimation of agglomeration. Moretti (local multipliers and sorting) and Gyourko (housing) also have strong claims, so any three-person selection leaves out important contributors. The field is also dispersed.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1990 to the present, and many results have been replicated. Prior recognition of the new economic geography (Krugman) overlaps in part.
uncertainties: Fragmented credit across a diffuse field.
Overlap with Krugman's earlier prize.
Whether any single discovery rises to the level of the leading candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy models of protection explain why trade policy departs from efficiency, and the Grossman–Helpman framework linked special-interest politics to measurable policy outcomes. It is a clear theoretical contribution with empirical follow-up, though narrower in scope than the leading candidates.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are the natural pair for the protection-for-sale framework. Helpman also appears in another candidate on firm heterogeneity, so his credit may be split across ballots.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the 1990s and has been tested extensively, with mixed empirical support for some predictions.
uncertainties: Mixed empirical performance of the protection-for-sale predictions.
Helpman's overlapping credit with the firm-heterogeneity candidate.
Smaller scope and policy impact than the higher-ranked candidates.
